links.reason: Both judge the departure for wealth: 43 calls the leavers pitiable and without அளி (அளிஇன்று ... மடமையோரே), and 53 gives his motive as a heart that cannot hide what it has from the needy (இல்லோர்க்கு இல் என்று இயைவது கரத்தல் வல்லா நெஞ்சம்). But the heroine of 53 reaches the same verdict as 43 (நம்மினும் பொருளே காதலர் காதல்); only the friend's அருளே காதலர் is opposed, so this is a qualification of motive, not two incompatible claims.

The patikam line (விஞ்சைக்கு இறைவன் மகள் வீணையில் தோற்றவாறும்) only announces the contest that 659 begins to narrate; nothing in 659 contradicts it, and 659 itself shows only birds flying off as if mocking (அசிப்ப போன்று) the faultless players. Summary and episode in story order are sequence, and the tension type has no incompatible claim to rest on.

1915 has Vijayai give Sunandai the name of mother (ஔவை யாவாள் சுநந்தையே); 2646 is a grieving outcry at her renunciation (சுநந்தை நீ ஔவை அல்லை, கொடியை), likely by Nandattan, her own son. A cry of reproach in grief is not a claim about who is mother, so the pair joins two verses by the shared word ஔவை, and the speaker of 2646 is itself uncertain.
links.text_issue: 2646: speaker not fixed by the verse (marker flagged uncertain).

links.reason: 409 foretells that within a month Tivittan will split a lion's mouth (திங்கள் நாள் அகவையில் திவிட்டன் ... சிங்கம் வாய் பிளந்திடும்), and verse 2 is the poet's announcement of the hero who tore the lion (அரியேறு போழ்ந்த செங்கண் நெடியான்). The real answer to the prophecy is the later killing, not the prologue; pairing prologue and prophecy adds little, and the claim that 409 is the first foretelling is not checked by the pair.
links.text_issue: soolamani:2 line 1 கணிவான்சுடர may be a misprint for அணிவான்சுடர்.

links.reason: 1803 does recall the king's reading (முன்னுரைத்த மூன்று கனவும் புணையாக என்னுயிரைத் தாங்கி இருந்தேன்), which answers 225, where he explains the crown and stops (பின்னதனால் பயன் பேசலன் விட்டான்). But nothing in 1803 touches the withheld part, so the teaches clause that the omitted omen 'proves the part she could not afford to hear' is the linker's construction, not the verse's.
links.text_issue: 1803 line 4: whether என்னரசே ... இறந்தனையே addresses the dead king or the son is unclear.

links.reason: The epic states the cause (தொல்வினை துரப்ப ஓடி விலங்கிடைச் சுழன்ற), and the Siddhar wishes to be done with births as stone, tree, fish, bird and grass (சென்மம் போதும் என்பது எக்காலம்). That is a shared theme of rebirth among lower kinds; 34 says nothing of a cry of 'enough' that the pair will act on, so the teaches sentence overstates what the verse does.
links.text_issue: yasodhara_kaviyam:34 line 1 மன்னை is doubtful (perhaps அன்னை).

links.reason: 1552 states only the prince's elation with no foe, wife, earth and Fortune (செருக்கிய களியன் ஆனான்); the teaches sentence itself concedes 'the verse says no such thing' about karma. Naladiyar 93's claim (விடுக்கும் வினையுலந்தக் கால்) is imported onto a verse that neither tests nor illustrates it.

1165 describes a warrior as born of the fire of anger with pride (சினமெனப் பட்ட தீயுள் பிறந்தது செருக்கு) in praise of martial fury; Tirumanthiram 266 condemns மலிந்தவர், whose sense (wealth or pride) is itself uncertain, as falling into மெலிந்த சினம். The link rests on reading மலிந்தவர் as the proud and the epic's heroic anger as the same vice.
links.text_issue: tirumanthiram:266 மெலிந்த சினம் is obscure.

links.reason: The words do touch: Vijayai's யாரையும் தேறன்மின் matches the Kural's first clause தேறற்க யாரையும், and the pair notes that she keeps only that clause. But the couplet concerns choosing men after examination (தேர்ந்தபின் தேறுக), while 1815 is about guarding one secret (இப்பொருள் யாதும் கூறின்மின்); a different situation gives different advice, so the qualification is thin.

If the friend who lifted the great trouble (பேரிடர் தன்கண் நீக்கிய தோழற்கு) is the god who was once the dog of 945, the gold image and dance repay the mantra of 945 (மந்திரம் ஐந்தும் ... செவிச் செப்புகின்றான்). The verse does not name him, the repayment runs through the rescue rather than the mantra, and 'the first public memorial the epic records' cannot be checked from the pair.
links.text_issue: 2573 line 1 நீக்கிப் யாய is corrupt (for நீக்கிய); 945 line 4 குதற்செய்கை is unclear.

links.reason: 106 gives the king's reason for leaving as karma (நிற்கும் செவ்வினை நீங்க நின்றனர்), not death or impermanence; Naladiyar 21 says only that no crowned king has been left over (எஞ்சினார் இவ்வுலகத்தில் இல்). The abdication as an answer to the quatrain's transience is the linker's motive, not the verse's, so the pair shares only the theme of kings leaving rule.
links.text_issue: naga_kumara_kaviyam:106 செவ்வினை and the subject of நின்றனர் are not fixed.

links.reason: The usurper, not seeing what is to come (நிகழ்வது ஓரான்), praises the returned mounts as twice his own gift, which fits the couplet's warning about foes like kin (கேள்போல் பகைவர் தொடர்பு). But 2175 shows a returned gift, not a bond of kinship, and its reading as bait rests on the plot outside the verse, so the case is suggestive rather than shown.
links.text_issue: 2175 marked uncertain; joined from 8 half-lines.

links.reason: 899 sets the condition: she will keep her vow until he comes defeated and worships her anklet feet (தோற்று வந்து என் சிலம்படி கைதொழ). 2088 shows him with his head on her anklets (சிலம்பின்மேல் சென்னி சேர்த்தி), pleading as the small who erred before the great (சிறியவர் செய்த தீமை ... பொறுப்பர் பெரியவர்), and her sulk ends. The later verse answers the earlier in its own terms, and the teaches clause names the change from contest to love-rite.

Both start from crowned heads come to nothing (மத்தக மாண்பழிதல் / முடிசார்ந்த மன்னரும் ... பிடிசாம்பராய்), and they part on the remedy: steady effort in the highest path leading to சித்தி, against reaching the feet of the Lord of the golden hall (பொன்னினம்பலவர் அடிசார்ந்து). The fragment never says that effort suffices without grace, so the incompatibility is supplied by school, as the teaches sentence concedes; and the bridge gives no gains.
links.text_issue: No gains clause given for this bridge.

links.reason: The women's நோற்றனள் ... நுகர்தற்கு does take penance as the merit behind a fine husband, and Kural 265 offers getting what is wanted (வேண்டிய வேண்டியாங்கு எய்தலால்) as the motive for தவம். But the women use a common idiom and do not recall the couplet, so the other-side gain ('evidence of how the couplet was heard') is unsupported.

1992 already ties the worth of a gift to a faultless receiver (உலைவில் ஏற்போன்), and Tirumanthiram 505 says giving to those without சீலமும் நோன்பும் is wasted. The two agree that the receiver's worth counts; the epic gaining 'a limit it does not name' is untrue, since உலைவில் ஏற்போன் already names it.

Cintamani 61 opens on the Sangam figure (கிணை நிலைப் பொருநர் தம் செல்லல் கீழ்ப்பட) and lets carts of paddy, cane and flowers lay it low, while the Sirupanarruppadai paints the kinai woman boiling unsalted greens behind a shut door (உப்பிலி வெந்ததை ... கடையடைத்து) until a patron's elephants and chariots end the hunger. The pair shows the epic keeping the bard's want only as a half-line and moving its relief from a giver to the land's plenty.

In 2149 Govindan says Kattiyangaran plotted to kill 'us' by guile (கள்ளத்தால் நம்மைக் கொல்லக் கருதினான்), which points to the plot against Govindan's own side, not to the usurpation of 259. 259 is an open declaration to Dharmadattan (மன்னன் போய்த் துறக்கம் ஆண்டு ... யான் காப்பல்), not guile, so the symmetry 'Govindan names outright' is not the one the note draws.

Both say goodness is wasted on the base: Pazhamozhi's tick plucked from a tiger's face (புலிமுகத்து உண்ணி பறித்து விடல்) and Sirupanchamoolam's good meat in a dog's mouth (நாய்வாயுள் நல்ல தசை). Sirupanchamoolam's dog has already bitten and risen barking, so it too carries danger, and the split into 'wasted' versus 'dangerous' does not hold.
links.text_issue: sirupanchamoolam:16 line 3 is hard to construe.

links.reason: In 3081 the fire is only a simile for the arrow of white meditation (இணர் எரி முழக்கம் அன்ன சுக்கிலத் தியானம் என்னுங் கணை); Tirumanthiram 219 has the kindled fire burn deeds (அங்கி வினைசுடும்). Both have deeds destroyed, and a difference in means of burning is not an incompatible claim about release; the 'Jain fire' of the gains clause is a figure of speech.
links.text_issue: tirumanthiram:219 வீழிசெய்து is obscure.

links.reason: The patikam line (அன்றைப் பகலே குணமாலையை அச்சுறுத்த வென்றிக் களிற்றை ... வென்றவாறும்) is summary, and 985 is the episode's close, Civakan victorious and going to the garden; summary to event is sequence. The teaches clause rests on verses 974-984, outside the pair, since 985 shows a feat, not mercy.
links.text_issue: 985 is in a longer metre than its neighbours; the count ஐஞ்ஞாற்று நால்வர் is uncertain.

links.reason: 73 shows Yugi preparing coded mad talk (மன்னவன் அறியும் மருளுரை) and a fixed disguise, and Kural 585 wants a form that raises no suspicion (கடாஅ உருவொடு). A madman is conspicuous but not suspected, which is just what the couplet asks for, so the 'exception' is not one; and the verse never says the guise draws every eye.

1040 is the maiden's prayer that the disease of birth leave her (பிறவிநோய் பெயர்க); 1107 is onlookers at the wedding, some going to forest penance and some turning back (மாதவம் போகுவாரும் ... கண்டுமீள்வாரும்). Nothing in either is incompatible with the other, and the 'two answers' are the linker's frame.
links.text_issue: soolamani:1107 marked uncertain.

links.reason: The lamp image is shared closely: Naladiyar 51 has darkness rush back when the lamp's oil wastes (விளக்குநெய் தேய்விடத்து) as evil settles when good deeds end, and 2316 has the flame dwindle when ghee and wick are spent (நெய்யும் திரியும் சென்று அற்ற போழ்தே) as wealth goes when the two deeds wear away (இருவினை சென்று தேய்ந்தால்). The pair shows the image moved from austerity to the fall of wealth and rule, with both kinds of deed as fuel, and the note claims no quotation.

647's first clause, not making foes of those who are not foes (பகையலாதவரைப் பகையாக்கலும்), agrees with Kural 871's refusal of enmity even in jest (நகையேயும் வேண்டற்பாற்று அன்று); the verse adds befriending the ill-hearted. This is agreement with an added item, not a limit, and the teaches sentence's 'two readings of Kural 879 and 871 as rival counsel' rests on a couplet and on counsel not in the packet.
links.text_issue: soolamani:647 line 2 word for the ill-hearted is corrupt.

links.reason: 908 has Suramanjari shut herself away save for Civakan (அன்றி என்னிறை யார் அழிப்பார்), and 1050 has Gunamalai name death or penance if her parents refuse him (இறத்தல் ஒன்றோ ... செய்தவம் முயறல் ஒன்றோ). The two vows run side by side from one contest; neither answers or fulfils the other, so develops is the wrong type for a parallel.

109 has the court affirm that Tivittan will guard the world under one umbrella (ஒருகுடை நீழல் காக்கும்); 722 describes only the lion swelling with might and the gods trembling (பனிவிசும்புடையவர் பனித்தார்), with no mention of Tivittan or his rule. The link joins a prophecy to a later scene by plot sequence alone.

The epic's மிறைக்கொளி(இ) திருத்துவான் matches Purananuru 284's எயிறு மிறையாகத் திரிந்த வாய்வாள் திருத்தா: the same act of straightening a bent sword against a lever, followed by the enemy's flight (அஞ்சி ... அரசர் ... இரிந்திட்டாரே / இரிந்தானைப் பெயர்புறம் நகுமே). The pair shows a Sangam war vignette taken over, with the laugh at the fleeing back turned into the foe's fear.
links.text_issue: 2293 line 3 prints மிறைக்கொளி, read as மிறைக்கொளீஇ; line 2 வான் புண்ணுள் நீட்டி is unclear.

links.reason: 2906 ranks guarding the earth and dharma as a king's highest joy (மேல்விளையாத இன்பம் வேந்த மற்றில்லை), and 2922 only asks the wives to steady their minds and hear the lasting good (உலவுமனம் வைத்து உறுதி கேண்மின்), without saying what it is. The qualification is implied by the speaker's coming renunciation, not stated by either verse.

1556 has the king caught in the net of deer-eyed women (மகளிர்தம் வலையிற் பட்டான்) and 1624 has him pierced by eye-arrows from brow-bows (புருவ வில்லால் ... பகழியால் அழுத்தப் பட்டான்). That is the poem repeating one figure of capture; the 'quarrel's cause' in the teaches sentence is not in either verse.

42 has even the lords of the gods lose their forms (இமையவர் இறைவரேனும் தந்திருவுருவம் பொன்றித் தளர்ந்தனர்), and Naladiyar 21 says no crowned king is left (எஞ்சினார் இவ்வுலகத்தில் இல்). The extension from kings to gods is real but it is the standard impermanence topic, and the pair teaches little beyond it.

1136 says Arimanju feared and hid the news that scorched the Vidyadhara world (வெய்துற விரிந்த மாற்றம் அஞ்சினன் மறைத்து) and had another report it. The verse makes the news, not the king's temper, the object of his fear, so reading it as the cost of a king who cannot bear bitter words (Kural 389, செவிகைப்பச் சொற்பொறுக்கும்) needs a generous reading.
links.text_issue: 1136 may still be the spy's report (marker's note).

links.reason: The stag that gives its shadow to the shadeless doe is shared closely: Kalittokai 11's இன்நிழல் இன்மையான் வருந்திய மடப்பிணைக்குத் தன் நிழலைக் கொடுத்து அளிக்கும் கலை and 1188's இலையின் நிழல் ... இன்மையினால் ... நின்று கொடுத்து. But the teaches sentence's 'lone traveller with no beloved at home' is untrue of Civakan, who by this book has already married, so the contrast it draws between uses is partly false.
links.text_issue: Only 1188 is printed; the elephant and bird of 1187 are taken on trust.

links.reason: 1435 claims that once loosed in hate the weapon does not turn back and no one can turn it (மறிதல் இல்லை மறிப்பவர் பிறரும் இல்லை), and 1439 has the deity bent on hostility (சலம்புரி தெய்வம்) take fright and return to its own shape. That is a claim and a scene that answers it, but the identity of the deity with the missile rests on reading சலம், and returning to its shape is not the same as being turned back.
links.text_issue: 1435 and 1439 both marked uncertain; change of speaker in 1435 line 4 unmarked.

links.reason: 57's elephant is maddened with anger (நாகம் மிக்க கதம் கொண்டு), not rut; the word மதம் on which the teaches sentence builds its double sense does not appear in the verse. The pairing with Tirumanthiram 2023's five rutting elephants of the senses (ஆக மதத்தன ஐந்து களிறு) rests only on the elephant.

The king resolves to offer a faultless human pair with his sword so that others may worship with animals (ஈனமில் பலியாக இயற்றினால் ... விலங்கினில் ஆன பூசனை ஆற்றுதல் ஆறு), and Kural 259 puts not killing and eating one creature above a thousand oblations (அவிசொரிந்து ஆயிரம் வேட்டலின் ... உயிர்செகுத்து உண்ணாமை நன்று). Killing as the right worship and non-killing above every rite are incompatible on the stated reading, and the note gives the claim to the king rather than to the work.
links.text_issue: yasodhara_kaviyam:21 speaker inferred from யான்.

links.reason: Purananuru 26 has the victor cook the field with crowned heads for a hearth and blood for water (முடித்தலை அடுப்பாக, புனல் குருதி உலைக் கொளீஇ, அடுகளம் வேட்ட), and 2235 turns to the slain, whose wedding garlands strung by their brides (மணமாலை மடந்தையர் ... தொடுத்து அணிந்த) give way to entrail garlands at the ghoul-woman's feast (நிணமாலைக் குடர்சூடி ... பேய்மகட்குப் பெருவிருந்து). The pair names what the epic changes in the battlefield-feast, the point of view and the cost in marriages.

388 makes the title இறை conditional on just rule (முறைசெய்து காப்பாற்றும் மன்னவன்), and 698 asks conduct in keeping with the light the ruler stands in (நின்ற ஒளியோடு ஒழுகப்படும்). The conflict depends on a commentator's gloss of ஒளி as divine light, and the teaches sentence ('other readings remove the conflict') undoes the link instead of saying what it teaches.

1357 shames those who flee to save their lives at the cost of honour (மான மாமணி வீழ்த்து உயிர்க்கு ... ஓடுவீர்), and 1380 calls the manhood of a man with a drawn sword who runs from one man loathsome (அருவருப்புடையது அவ்வாண்மை). Two taunts at flight in different scenes say the same thing; neither develops the other.
links.text_issue: 1357 lines 3-4 are obscure.

links.reason: The note says both ask whether the woman is 'a goddess, a rare bird or a human', but 1017's three are a gods' daughter, a Vidyadhara woman or one of earth (வானவர் மகள்கொல் விஞ்சை மாதுகொல் மண்ணுளாள்கொல்); there is no bird. The Kural's three are அணங்கு, ஆய்மயில், மாதர். The three-way doubt is a shared form, but the note misdescribes the epic verse on its central point.

1585 has Civakan call the body a painted bag of skin dressed up by the kavya poets to light desire (காப்பியக் கவிகள் காம எரியெழ விகற்பித்திட்டார்), and 1482 has him lament that her hair, brows, eyes and breasts kill him (இளமுலை கொல்லும் கொல்லுமே). The irony is real, but the two are a lover's cry and a renunciant's lesson in different situations, which is not an incompatible claim, as the teaches clause itself allows.

1798 shows the kings' desire swelling as Sayambavai enters (அவர்கள் காதல் மிக வீங்க), with no word of age or warning; Naladiyar 17's staff-eyed old woman (கோல்கண்ணள் ஆகும் குனிந்து) is set on the scene from outside. The gains clause itself says the limit is 'not stated' by the verse.
links.text_issue: 1798 line 1 சராவி is a rare or damaged word.

links.reason: 1177 has the Caranas wash away their own karma (தம்வினை கழுவுகின்றார் சாரணர்) by turning from the cruelty of rule and renouncing, while Tirumanthiram 2422 makes the washer's soiling of cloth to clean it (அறுவை அழுக்கேற்றி ஏற்றல்போல்) the work of grace, all that comes to the soul being அருட்பாசம். Self-cleansing by austerity and cleansing as grace's work are rival claims about the same release, which is the tension this round tests.
links.text_issue: tirumanthiram:2422 மோசு is obscure; the verse is marked uncertain.
